intent: Stop .scratch/ (agent working files and a headless-Chrome profile that may hold cookies) from ever being committed by a broad git add.
summary: PSI-124: .scratch/ was untracked but not ignored, and holds .scratch/cdp-profile (660 files: extension JS, LevelDB) that may contain cookies and session tokens, so one git add -A or git add . from any agent would have committed a live browser profile. Added PSI-124 to docs/list-task-project.md (Phase 0, backlog, then claimed and set to review) because C-01 requires a card for every session, then added a commented .scratch/ rule to .gitignore (CRLF preserved) next to the .ecc/ entry. Verified: git check-ignore -v .scratch/cdp-profile prints .gitignore:21, and git status no longer lists .scratch/. The profile itself was left in place: the operator may still be running the headless-Chrome session that owns it, so deleting it is their call. Not done here: Priority 1 of the operator brief (re-render obsidian-out after the PSI-123/PSI-119 merge) is blocked until one of PRs #76 and #77 merges; Priority 3 items wait for the operator to choose.
